Kikuyu: Matukũ-inĩ ma tene Ngai nĩarĩirie maithe maitũ na tũnua twa anabii maita maingĩ, na njĩra mwanya mwanya,
English: God, having in the past spoken to the fathers through the prophets at many times and in various ways,

Kikuyu: no matukũ-inĩ maya ma kũrigĩrĩria-rĩ, ithuĩ nĩatwarĩirie na njĩra ya Mũriũ, ũrĩa aatuire mũgai wa indo ciothe, o we ũrĩa thĩ yothe yombirwo na ũndũ wake.
English: has at the end of these days spoken to us by his Son, whom he appointed heir of all things, through whom also he made the worlds.

Kikuyu: Mũrũwe-rĩ, nĩwe wonanagia ũkengi wa riiri wake, na nĩwe mũhianĩre mũkinyanĩru kũna wa ũrĩa Ngai atariĩ, ningĩ nĩwe ũnyiitĩrĩire indo ciothe na kiugo gĩake kĩrĩ hinya. Nake aarĩkia gũtheria andũ mehia-rĩ, nĩaikarire thĩ guoko-inĩ kwa ũrĩo kwa Ũnene kũu igũrũ.
English: His Son is the radiance of his glory, the very image of his substance, and upholding all things by the word of his power, who, when he had by himself purified us of our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high,

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio agĩtuĩka mũnene gũkĩra araika, o ta ũrĩa rĩĩtwa rĩrĩa aagaĩirwo rĩrĩ inene gũkĩra rĩao.
English: having become as much better than the angels as the more excellent name he has inherited is better than theirs.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ-rĩ, nĩ mũraika ũrĩkũ Ngai arĩ eera atĩrĩ, “Wee nĩwe Mũrũ wakwa; ũmũthĩ nĩndatuĩka Thoguo”? O na kana akĩmwĩra atĩrĩ, “Nĩ niĩ ngũtuĩka Ithe, nake atuĩke Mũrũ wakwa”?
English: For to which of the angels did he say at any time, “You are my Son. Today I have become your father?”* and again, “I will be to him a Father, and he will be to me a Son?”*

Kikuyu: Na ningĩ-rĩ, Ngai aarehe irigithathi rĩake gũkũ thĩ, oigire atĩrĩ, “Araika othe a Ngai nĩmamũinamĩrĩre, mamũhooe.”
English: When he again brings in the firstborn into the world he says, “Let all the angels of God worship him.”*

Kikuyu: Akĩaria ũhoro wa araika oigire atĩrĩ, “Atũmaga araika ake matuĩke huho, nacio ndungata ciake agacitua nĩnĩmbĩ cia mwaki.”
English: Of the angels he says, “He makes his angels winds, and his servants a flame of fire.”*

Kikuyu: No ha ũhoro ũkoniĩ Mũriũ ekuuga atĩrĩ, “Wee Ngai, gĩtĩ gĩaku kĩa ũnene nĩgĩgatũũra tene na tene, nakĩo kĩhooto nĩkĩo gĩgaatuĩka mũthĩgi wa ũthamaki waku.
English: But of the Son he says, “Your throne, O God, is forever and ever. The scepter of uprightness is the scepter of your Kingdom.

Kikuyu: Wee wendete ũthingu no ũgathũũra waganu; nĩ ũndũ ũcio, Ngai, o we Ngai waku, nĩakwambararĩtie gũkĩra athiritũ aku othe na ũndũ wa gũgũitĩrĩria maguta ma gĩkeno.”
English: You have loved righteousness and hated iniquity; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your fellows.”*

Kikuyu: Ningĩ akoiga atĩrĩ, “Wee Mwathani, o kĩambĩrĩria-inĩ, nĩwaarire mĩthingi ya thĩ, o narĩo igũrũ nĩ wĩra wa moko maku.
English: And, “You, Lord, in the beginning, laid the foundation of the earth. The heavens are the works of your hands.

Kikuyu: Icio nĩgũthira igaathira, no wee nĩgũtũũra ũgaatũũra; igaathira o ta nguo.
English: They will perish, but you continue. They all will grow old like a garment does.

Kikuyu: Ũgaacikũnja o ta ũrĩa nguo ndaaya ikũnjagwo; ikaagarũrũka o ta ũrĩa nguo igarũrũkaga. No wee ndũgarũrũkaga, na mĩaka yaku ndĩrĩ hĩndĩ ĩgaathira.”
English: You will roll them up like a mantle, and they will be changed; but you are the same. Your years won’t fail.”*

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ-rĩ, nĩ mũraika ũrĩkũ Ngai arĩ eera atĩrĩ, “Ikara thĩ guoko-inĩ gwakwa kwa ũrĩo, nginya rĩrĩa ngaatũma thũ ciaku ituĩke gaturwa ka makinya maku”?
English: But which of the angels has he told at any time, “Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet?”*

Kikuyu: Githĩ araika othe ti maroho ma gũtungata, matũmĩtwo matungatagĩre arĩa makaagaya ũhonokio?
English: Aren’t they all serving spirits, sent out to do service for the sake of those who will inherit salvation?

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio-rĩ, nĩtwagĩrĩirwo kũrũmbũiya mũno ũhoro ũrĩa twanaigua, nĩguo tũtikae gũtũgũgio tweherio kuuma harĩ guo.
English: Therefore we ought to pay greater attention to the things that were heard, lest perhaps we drift away.

Kikuyu: Tondũ-rĩ, angĩkorwo ũhoro ũrĩa waririo nĩ araika warĩ mũrũmu-rĩ, na mũndũ o wothe wareganaga na ũhoro ũcio na akaũremera nĩaherithagio o ũrĩa kwagĩrĩire-rĩ,
English: For if the word spoken through angels proved steadfast, and every transgression and disobedience received a just penalty,

Kikuyu: tũngĩkĩaga atĩa kũherithio tũngĩnyarara ũhonokio mũnene ũũ? Ũhonokio ũyũ, ũrĩa waambire kũhunjio nĩ Mwathani, nĩwacookire gwĩkĩrwo hinya kũrĩ ithuĩ nĩ andũ arĩa maamũiguire.
English: how will we escape if we neglect so great a salvation—which at the first having been spoken through the Lord, was confirmed to us by those who heard,

Kikuyu: Ningĩ Ngai agĩĩkĩra ũhoro ũyũ ũira atĩ nĩ wa ma na ũndũ wa kuonania marũũri na morirũ, o na kũringa ciama cia mĩthemba mĩingĩ, na akĩheana iheo cia Roho Mũtheru kũrĩ andũ kũringana na wendi wake.
English: God also testifying with them, both by signs and wonders, by various works of power, and by gifts of the Holy Spirit, according to his own will?

Kikuyu: Thĩ ĩrĩa tũkwaria ũhoro wayo, araika tio maaheetwo wathani wayo.
English: For he didn’t subject the world to come, of which we speak, to angels.

Kikuyu: No nĩ harĩ mũndũ mũna ũheanĩte ũira handũ hamwe akoiga atĩrĩ: “Mũndũ akĩrĩ kĩ tondũ ũikaraga ũkĩmwĩciiragia, nake mũrũ wa mũndũ akĩrĩ kĩ atĩ nĩkĩo ũmũmenyagĩrĩra?
English: But one has somewhere testified, saying, “What is man, that you think of him? Or the son of man, that you care for him?

Kikuyu: Watũmire atigie o hanini aiganane na araika, na ũkĩmũhumba thũmbĩ ya riiri o na gĩtĩĩo,
English: You made him a little lower than the angels. You crowned him with glory and honor.†

Kikuyu: na ũkĩiga indo ciothe rungu rwa magũrũ make aciathage.” Nake akĩiga indo ciothe rungu rwa mũndũ-rĩ, hatirĩ kĩndũ o na kĩrĩkũ Ngai aatigire gĩtarĩ watho- inĩ wa mũndũ. No rĩu tũtionaga indo ciothe irĩ watho-inĩ wa mũndũ.
English: You have put all things in subjection under his feet.”* For in that he subjected all things to him, he left nothing that is not subject to him. But now we don’t yet see all things subjected to him.

Kikuyu: No tuonaga Jesũ, ũrĩa gwa kahinda kanini watuĩtwo mũnini gũkĩra araika, no rĩu ekĩrĩtwo thũmbĩ ya riiri na ya gĩtĩĩo nĩ tondũ nĩanyariirĩkire na agĩkua, nĩgeetha, nĩ ũndũ wa Wega wa Ngai atuĩke wa gũcama gĩkuũ handũ ha andũ othe.
English: But we see him who has been made a little lower than the angels, Jesus, because of the suffering of death crowned with glory and honor, that by the grace of God he should taste of death for everyone.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo nĩ kwagĩrĩire atĩ Ngai, ũrĩa wombire indo ciothe na itũũraga nĩ ũndũ wake-rĩ, atũme mwambĩrĩria wa ũhonokio wao aagĩrĩre kũna kũna na ũndũ wa kũnyamario nĩguo arehe ciana nyingĩ riiri-inĩ wake.
English: For it became him, for whom are all things and through whom are all things, in bringing many children to glory, to make the author of their salvation perfect through sufferings.

Kikuyu: Jesũ ũrĩa ũtũmaga andũ matuĩke atheru, o hamwe na acio matuĩtwo atheru, othe matuĩkaga andũ a nyũmba ĩmwe. Nĩ ũndũ ũcio Jesũ ndaconokaga akĩmeeta ariũ na aarĩ a Ithe.
English: For both he who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are all from one, for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brothers,‡

Kikuyu: Akoiga atĩrĩ, “Nĩngoimbũra rĩĩtwa rĩaku kũrĩ ariũ na aarĩ a Baba; nĩngainaga nyĩmbo cia gũkũgooca ndĩ kĩũngano-inĩ.”
English: saying, “I will declare your name to my brothers. Among the congregation I will sing your praise.”*

Kikuyu: Ningĩ akoiga atĩrĩ, “Niĩ ngũiga mwĩhoko wakwa harĩ Ngai.” O na ningĩ akoiga atĩrĩ, “Niĩ ũyũ haha, na ciana iria Ngai aaheete.”
English: Again, “I will put my trust in him.” Again, “Behold, here I am with the children whom God has given me.”*

Kikuyu: Kuona atĩ ciana icio irĩ na mwĩrĩ na thakame-rĩ, we o nake aatuĩkire o tao mwĩrĩ-inĩ, nĩgeetha na ũndũ wa gĩkuũ gĩake ahote kwananga ũrĩa ũrĩ na hinya wa gĩkuũ, nake nĩwe mũcukani,
English: Since then the children have shared in flesh and blood, he also himself in the same way partook of the same, that through death he might bring to nothing him who had the power of death, that is, the devil,

Kikuyu: na ohore arĩa matũire mohetwo ũkombo-inĩ matukũ mao mothe nĩ ũndũ wa gwĩtigĩra gĩkuũ.
English: and might deliver all of them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo ti-itherũ ti araika ateithagia, no ateithagia rũciaro rwa Iburahĩmu.
English: For most certainly, he doesn’t give help to angels, but he gives help to the offspring§ of Abraham.

Kikuyu: Na nĩ ũndũ ũcio no nginya angĩahaananirio na ariũ na aarĩ a Ithe maũndũ-inĩ mothe, nĩguo atuĩke mũthĩnjĩri-Ngai ũrĩa mũnene ũiyũrĩtwo nĩ tha na mwĩhokeku agĩtungatĩra Ngai, na nĩguo arute horohio nĩ ũndũ wa mehia ma kĩrĩndĩ.
English: Therefore he was obligated in all things to be made like his brothers, that he might become a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make atonement for the sins of the people.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo we mwene nĩathĩĩnĩkire rĩrĩa aageragio-rĩ, nĩahotaga gũteithia andũ arĩa mageragio.
English: For in that he himself has suffered being tempted, he is able to help those who are tempted.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio, inyuĩ ariũ na aarĩ a Ithe witũ atheru, o inyuĩ mũgwatanĩire ũhoro wa gwĩtwo kũrĩa kuumĩte na igũrũ, mwĩcũranagiei ũhoro wa Jesũ, o we mũtũmwo na mũthĩnjĩri-Ngai ũrĩa mũnene ũrĩa tuumbũraga ũhoro wake.
English: Therefore, holy brothers, partakers of a heavenly calling, consider the Apostle and High Priest of our confession: Jesus,

Kikuyu: We aarĩ mwĩhokeku kũrĩ ũrĩa wamwamũrire, o ta ũrĩa Musa aarĩ mwĩhokeku maũndũ-inĩ mothe ma nyũmba ya Ngai.
English: who was faithful to him who appointed him, as also Moses was in all his house.

Kikuyu: Jesũ nĩonekanĩte aagĩrĩire kũheo gĩtĩĩo kĩnene gũkĩra Musa, o ta ũrĩa mwaki wa nyũmba aagĩrĩirwo nĩ gũtĩĩo gũkĩra nyũmba yo nyene.
English: For he has been counted worthy of more glory than Moses, because he who built the house has more honor than the house.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo nyũmba o yothe nĩĩrĩ mũndũ ũrĩa wamĩakire, no Ngai nĩwe mwaki wa indo ciothe.
English: For every house is built by someone; but he who built all things is God.

Kikuyu: Nake Musa, aarĩ mwĩhokeku maũndũ-inĩ mothe ma nyũmba ya Ngai arĩ o ndungata, agakĩrutaga ũira wa maũndũ marĩa makaaheanwo thuutha-inĩ.
English: Moses indeed was faithful in all his house as a servant, for a testimony of those things which were afterward to be spoken,

Kikuyu: No Kristũ arĩ Mũriũ aarĩ mwĩhokeku na akarũgamĩrĩra nyũmba ya Ngai. Na ithuĩ tũrĩ nyũmba ĩyo yake, tũngĩikara tũrũmĩtie ũmĩrĩru witũ na kĩĩrĩgĩrĩro kĩrĩa twĩrahagĩra.
English: but Christ† is faithful as a Son over his house. We are his house, if we hold fast our confidence and the glorying of our hope firm to the end.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ-rĩ, o ta ũrĩa Roho Mũtheru oigaga, atĩrĩ: “Ũmũthĩ, mũngĩigua mũgambo wake,
English: Therefore, even as the Holy Spirit says, “Today if you will hear his voice,

Kikuyu: mũtikoomie ngoro cianyu ta hĩndĩ ĩrĩa mwanemeire, andũ makĩĩngeria marĩ kũu werũ-inĩ,
English: don’t harden your hearts as in the rebellion, in the day of the trial in the wilderness,

Kikuyu: kũrĩa maithe manyu maangeririe na makĩndoria, na makĩona ciĩko ciakwa, ihinda rĩa mĩaka mĩrongo ĩna.
English: where your fathers tested me and tried me, and saw my deeds for forty years.

Kikuyu: Nĩkĩo ndaarakarĩire rũciaro rũu, ngĩkiuga atĩrĩ, ‘Ngoro cia andũ aya itururaga hĩndĩ ciothe, na matirĩ maamenya njĩra ciakwa.’
English: Therefore I was displeased with that generation, and said, ‘They always err in their heart, but they didn’t know my ways.’

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio ngĩĩhĩta na mwĩhĩtwa ndakarĩte, ngiuga atĩrĩ, ‘Matirĩ hĩndĩ magaatoonya kĩhurũko-inĩ gĩakwa.’ ”
English: As I swore in my wrath, ‘They will not enter into my rest.’ ”*

Kikuyu: Ariũ na aarĩ a Ithe witũ, mwĩmenyererei hatikagĩe o na ũmwe wanyu ũrĩ na ngoro ĩĩhagia na ĩtetĩkagia, ĩrĩa ĩgarũrũkaga, ĩgatigana na Ngai ũrĩa ũrĩ muoyo.
English: Beware, brothers, lest perhaps there might be in any one of you an evil heart of unbelief, in falling away from the living God;

Kikuyu: No ũmanagĩrĩriai mũndũ na ũrĩa ũngĩ o mũthenya, o rĩrĩa rĩothe mũthenya ũrĩĩtagwo Ũmũthĩ, nĩgeetha gũtikagĩe o na ũmwe wanyu ũkũũmio ngoro nĩ ũndũ wa kũheenererio nĩ mehia.
English: but exhort one another day by day, so long as it is called “today”, lest any one of you be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.

Kikuyu: Tondũ ũcio, tũngĩrũmia wega mwĩhoko ũrĩa twarĩ naguo kuuma o kĩambĩrĩria nginya ithirĩro-rĩ, nĩtũgaatuĩka a kũgwatanĩra hamwe na Kristũ.
English: For we have become partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence firm to the end,

Kikuyu: O ta ũrĩa kwĩrĩtwo, atĩrĩ: “Ũmũthĩ, mũngĩigua mũgambo wake, mũtikoomie ngoro cianyu ta hĩndĩ ĩrĩa mwanemeire.”
English: while it is said, “Today if you will hear his voice, don’t harden your hearts, as in the rebellion.”*

Kikuyu: Nĩ andũ arĩkũ acio maaiguire na makĩmũkararia? Githĩ ti arĩa othe moimĩte Misiri matongoretio nĩ Musa?
English: For who, when they heard, rebelled? Wasn’t it all those who came out of Egypt led by Moses?

Kikuyu: Ningĩ-rĩ, nĩ andũ arĩkũ aarakarĩire mĩaka ĩyo mĩrongo ĩna? Githĩ ti arĩa meehirie, na magĩkua, o arĩa ciimba ciao ciagũire kũu werũ-inĩ?
English: With whom was he displeased forty years? Wasn’t it with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?

Kikuyu: Ningĩ-rĩ, nĩ andũ arĩkũ Ngai ehĩtire na mwĩhĩtwa atĩ gũtirĩ hĩndĩ magaatoonya ũhurũko-inĩ wake, tiga o andũ acio maaregire kũmwathĩkĩra?
English: To whom did he swear that they wouldn’t enter into his rest, but to those who were disobedient?

Kikuyu: Tũgakĩona atĩrĩ, matiahotire gũtoonya kuo nĩ ũndũ wa kwaga gwĩtĩkia kwao.
English: We see that they weren’t able to enter in because of unbelief.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio-rĩ, kuona atĩ kĩĩranĩro gĩa gũtoonya ũhurũko-inĩ wake kĩrĩ o ho-rĩ, nĩtwĩmenyererei gũtikagĩe o na ũmwe wanyu ũtagagĩkinyĩra.
English: Let’s fear therefore, lest perhaps anyone of you should seem to have come short of a promise of entering into his rest.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo o na ithuĩ nĩtũhunjĩirio Ũhoro-ũyũ-Mwega o tao; no ũhoro ũrĩa maaiguire ndũigana kũmaguna, tondũ arĩa maũiguire matiawamũkĩrire na wĩtĩkio.
English: For indeed we have had good news preached to us, even as they also did, but the word they heard didn’t profit them, because it wasn’t mixed with faith by those who heard.

Kikuyu: Na rĩrĩ, ithuĩ arĩa twĩtĩkĩtie nĩ ithuĩ tũtoonyaga kĩhurũko-inĩ kĩu, o ta ũrĩa Ngai oigire atĩrĩ, “Nĩ ũndũ ũcio ngĩĩhĩta na mwĩhĩtwa ndakarĩte, ngiuga atĩrĩ, ‘Matirĩ hĩndĩ magaatoonya kĩhurũko-inĩ gĩakwa.’ ” O na gũtuĩka wĩra wake nĩwathirĩte kuuma o rĩrĩa thĩ yombirwo.
English: For we who have believed do enter into that rest, even as he has said, “As I swore in my wrath, they will not enter into my rest;”* although the works were finished from the foundation of the world.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo nĩ harĩ handũ hana aarĩtie ũhoro wa mũthenya wa mũgwanja, akoiga atĩrĩ: “Nake Ngai akĩhurũka mũthenya wa mũgwanja, agĩtigana na wĩra wake wothe.”
English: For he has said this somewhere about the seventh day, “God rested on the seventh day from all his works;”*

Kikuyu: O na ningĩ hau mbere nĩoigĩte atĩrĩ, “Matirĩ hĩndĩ magaatoonya ũhurũko-inĩ wakwa.”
English: and in this place again, “They will not enter into my rest.”*

Kikuyu: Nĩtũkuona atĩ nĩ kũrĩ amwe matigaire gũtoonya kĩhurũko-inĩ kĩu kĩeranĩirwo, nĩgũkorwo arĩa maahunjĩirio Ũhoro-ũrĩa-Mwega mbere matiatoonyire tondũ nĩmagire gwathĩka.
English: Seeing therefore it remains that some should enter into it, and they to whom the good news was preached before failed to enter in because of disobedience,

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio, o rĩngĩ Ngai akĩamũra mũthenya mũna, akĩwĩĩta Ũmũthĩ, thuutha wa matukũ maingĩ gũthira rĩrĩa aaririe na kanua ka Daudi, ta ũrĩa oigĩte hau mbere atĩrĩ: “Ũmũthĩ, mũngĩigua mũgambo wake, mũtikoomie ngoro cianyu.”
English: he again defines a certain day, “today”, saying through David so long a time afterward (just as has been said), “Today if you will hear his voice, don’t harden your hearts.”*

Kikuyu: Tondũ korwo Joshua nĩamaheete ũhurũko-rĩ, Ngai ndangĩacookire kwaria ũhoro wa mũthenya ũngĩ thuutha ũcio.
English: For if Joshua had given them rest, he would not have spoken afterward of another day.

Kikuyu: Tondũ ũcio nĩgũtigaire Thabatũ ya kũhurũka ya andũ a Ngai;
English: There remains therefore a Sabbath rest for the people of God.

Kikuyu: nĩgũkorwo mũndũ o wothe ũrĩa ũtoonyaga kĩhurũko-inĩ kĩa Ngai o nake nĩahurũkaga agatigana na wĩra wake, o ta ũrĩa Ngai aahurũkire agĩtigana na wĩra wake.
English: For he who has entered into his rest has himself also rested from his works, as God did from his.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio, nĩtwĩrutanĩrie na kĩyo gũtoonya ũhurũko- inĩ ũcio, nĩgeetha gũtikanagĩe mũndũ o na ũrĩkũ ũkaagũa nĩ ũndũ wa kũrũmĩrĩra kĩonereria kĩa ũremi wao.
English: Let’s therefore give diligence to enter into that rest, lest anyone fall after the same example of disobedience.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo ũhoro wa Ngai ũrĩ muoyo na ũrĩ hinya. Nĩ mũũgĩ gũkĩra rũhiũ rwa njora rũnooretwo mĩena yeerĩ, ũgatheeca ũkagayũkania muoyo na roho, o na ũkagayania marũngo na maguta marĩa makoragwo mahĩndĩ-inĩ, na ningĩ ũgatuĩra meciiria na matua ma ngoro.
English: For the word of God is living and active, and sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing even to the dividing of soul and spirit, of both joints and marrow, and is able to discern the thoughts and intentions of the heart.

Kikuyu: Gũtirĩ kĩndũ o na kĩmwe kĩa iria ciombirwo kĩhithĩtwo kuuma maitho-inĩ ma Ngai. Indo ciothe nĩhumbũrie na ikaguũrio mbere ya maitho ma ũrĩa tũkaahe ũhoro witũ.
English: There is no creature that is hidden from his sight, but all things are naked and laid open before the eyes of him to whom we must give an account.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio, kuona atĩ tũrĩ na mũthĩnjĩri-Ngai mũnene mũno ũrĩa ũhungurĩte agakinya o igũrũ, na nĩwe Jesũ mũrũ wa Ngai-rĩ, nĩtũrũmiei na hinya wĩtĩkio ũrĩa tuumbũraga.
English: Having then a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus, the Son of God, let’s hold tightly to our confession.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo tũtirĩ na mũthĩnjĩri-Ngai mũnene ũtangĩhota gũtũiguĩra tha ũhũthũ-inĩ witũ, no nĩ tũrĩ na ũmwe wanagerio ikĩro-inĩ ciothe o ta ithuĩ, no ndaigana kwĩhia.
English: For we don’t have a high priest who can’t be touched with the feeling of our infirmities, but one who has been in all points tempted like we are, yet without sin.

Kikuyu: Hakĩrĩ ũguo-rĩ, nĩtũkuhĩrĩriei gĩtĩ kĩa Ũnene kĩrĩa kĩa Wega wake tũrĩ na ũũmĩrĩru, nĩgeetha tũkaiguĩrwo tha, na tuone Wega wake wa gũtũteithagia hĩndĩ ĩrĩa tũbatarĩte.
English: Let’s therefore draw near with boldness to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy and may find grace for help in time of need.

Kikuyu: Rĩu-rĩ, mũthĩnjĩri-Ngai ũrĩa mũnene o wothe athuuragwo kuuma gatagatĩ ka andũ na agatuuo wa kũmarũgamĩrĩra maũndũ-inĩ marĩa makoniĩ Ngai, nĩguo arutage maruta na magongona nĩ ũndũ wa kũhoroheria mehia.
English: For every high priest, being taken from among men, is appointed for men in things pertaining to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins.

Kikuyu: Nake nĩahotaga gũkirĩrĩria arĩa matarĩ na ũmenyo o na arĩa maturuurĩte, kuona atĩ o nake nĩarĩ ũhũthũ wake.
English: The high priest can deal gently with those who are ignorant and going astray, because he himself is also surrounded with weakness.

Kikuyu: Ũndũ ũyũ nĩguo ũtũmaga arute magongona ma kũhoroheria mehia make mwene, o ta ũrĩa amarutaga nĩ ũndũ wa mehia ma kĩrĩndĩ.
English: Because of this, he must offer sacrifices for sins for the people, as well as for himself.

Kikuyu: Gũtirĩ mũndũ wĩheaga gĩtĩĩo kĩu we mwene; no nginya akorwo etĩtwo nĩ Ngai, o ta ũrĩa Harũni eetirwo.
English: Nobody takes this honor on himself, but he is called by God, just like Aaron was.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio, o nake Kristũ ndaigana kwĩyoera ũgooci wa gũtuĩka mũthĩnjĩri-Ngai ũrĩa mũnene. No nĩ Ngai wamwĩrire atĩrĩ, “Wee nĩwe Mũrũ wakwa; ũmũthĩ nĩndatuĩka Thoguo.”
English: So also Christ didn’t glorify himself to be made a high priest, but it was he who said to him, “You are my Son. Today I have become your father.”*

Kikuyu: Na handũ hangĩ oigĩte atĩrĩ, “Wee ũrĩ mũthĩnjĩri-Ngai nginya tene, o ta ũrĩa Melikisedeki aatariĩ.”
English: As he says also in another place, “You are a priest forever, after the order of Melchizedek.”*

Kikuyu: Matukũ-inĩ marĩa Jesũ aatũũraga gũkũ thĩ-rĩ, nĩahooyaga na agathaitha Ngai, agĩkayaga mũno agĩitaga maithori kũrĩ ũcio ũngĩahotire kũmũhonokia kuuma gĩkuũ-inĩ, na nĩaiguagwo nĩ ũndũ wa kwĩnyiihia gwake.
English: He, in the days of his flesh, having offered up prayers and petitions with strong crying and tears to him who was able to save him from death, and having been heard for his godly fear,

Kikuyu: O na gũtuĩka aarĩ mũriũ, nĩerutire gwathĩka nĩ ũndũ wa ũrĩa aanyariirĩkire,
English: though he was a Son, yet learned obedience by the things which he suffered.

Kikuyu: na aarĩkia gũtuuo mwagĩrĩru kũna, agĩtuĩka kĩhumo kĩa ũhonokio ũrĩa ũtagaathira harĩ arĩa othe mamwathĩkagĩra,
English: Having been made perfect, he became to all of those who obey him the author of eternal salvation,

Kikuyu: nake Ngai akĩmũtua mũthĩnjĩri-Ngai mũnene o ta ũrĩa Melikisedeki aatariĩ.
English: named by God a high priest after the order of Melchizedek.

Kikuyu: Nĩtũrĩ na maũndũ maingĩ tũngĩmwĩra makoniĩ ũhoro ũyũ, no nĩ hinya kũmũtaarĩria tondũ mũtinyiitaga maũndũ narua.
English: About him we have many words to say, and hard to interpret, seeing you have become dull of hearing.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ-rĩ, o na gũtuĩka rĩu mwagĩrĩirwo nĩgũkorwo mũrĩ arutani-rĩ, nĩmũbatarĩte mũndũ wa kũmũruta maũndũ marĩa mwarutĩtwo kĩambĩrĩria ma kiugo kĩa Ngai o rĩngĩ. Inyuĩ mũbataire kũheo iria, no ti irio nyũmũ!
English: For although by this time you should be teachers, you again need to have someone teach you the rudiments of the first principles of the revelations of God. You have come to need milk, and not solid food.

Kikuyu: Mũndũ o wothe ũnyuuaga iria, tondũ no gakenge-rĩ, ndangĩmenya wega ũhoro wa ũrutani wa ũthingu.
English: For everyone who lives on milk is not experienced in the word of righteousness, for he is a baby.

Kikuyu: No irio iria nyũmũ nĩ cia andũ arĩa agima, arĩa nĩ ũndũ wa kũmenyera gũcihũthĩra kaingĩ, nĩmerutĩte gũkũũrana wega na ũũru.
English: But solid food is for those who are full grown, who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern good and evil.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio nĩtũtiganei na morutani marĩa ma kĩambĩrĩria ma ũhoro wa Kristũ, na tũthiĩ na mbere na gũkũra, na tũtige kwambĩrĩria gwaka mũthingi rĩngĩ wa kũrutana ũhoro wa kwĩrira nĩ ũndũ wa ciĩko iria cierekagĩria mũndũ gĩkuũ-inĩ, na ũrutani wa gwĩtĩkia thĩinĩ wa Ngai,
English: Therefore leaving the teaching of the first principles of Christ, let’s press on to perfection—not laying again a foundation of repentance from dead works, of faith toward God,

Kikuyu: na morutani ma ũbatithio, na ma kũigĩrĩrwo moko, o na ma kũriũka kwa arĩa akuũ, o na ma gũtuĩrwo ciira wa tene na tene.
English: of the teaching of baptisms, of laying on of hands, of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.

Kikuyu: Na noguo tũrĩĩkaga, Ngai angĩĩtĩkĩria.
English: This will we do, if God permits.

Kikuyu: Na rĩrĩ, nĩ ũndũ ũrĩ hinya mũno kũrĩ andũ arĩa maanathererwo nĩ ũtheri, na magacama kĩheo kĩrĩa kiumĩte igũrũ, na magakorwo matuĩtwo a ngwatanĩro ya Roho Mũtheru,
English: For concerning those who were once enlightened and tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Spirit,

Kikuyu: o acio macamĩte wega wa kiugo kĩa Ngai na maahinya ma ihinda rĩrĩa rĩgooka,
English: and tasted the good word of God and the powers of the age to come,

Kikuyu: andũ acio mangĩgũa na matigane na maũndũ macio-rĩ, gũtingĩhoteka kũmacookia rĩngĩ merire, nĩ tondũ nĩ kwambithia marambithia Mũrũ wa Ngai mũtĩ igũrũ o rĩngĩ, na makamũnyararithia kũrĩ kĩrĩndĩ.
English: and then fell away, it is impossible to renew them again to repentance; seeing they crucify the Son of God for themselves again, and put him to open shame.

Kikuyu: Mũgũnda ũrĩa uragĩrwo nĩ mbura kaingĩ na ũgacooka ũgaciara maciaro mega ma kũguna arĩa marĩmĩirwo-rĩ, nĩũrathimagwo nĩ Ngai.
English: For the land which has drunk the rain that comes often on it and produces a crop suitable for them for whose sake it is also tilled, receives blessing from God;

Kikuyu: No mũgũnda ũrĩa ũkũraga mĩigua na mahiũ ma nyeki-inĩ nĩ wa tũhũ, na ũrĩ ũgwati-inĩ wa kwĩrehithĩria kĩrumi. Marigĩrĩrio-inĩ nĩgũcinwo ũgaacinwo.
English: but if it bears thorns and thistles, it is rejected and near being cursed, whose end is to be burned.

Kikuyu: Arata akwa nyendete mũno, o na tũkĩaragia ũguo, ha ũhoro wanyu-rĩ, nĩtwĩrĩgĩrĩire maũndũ mega kũrĩ macio, o marĩa marehanaga na ũhonokio.
English: But, beloved, we are persuaded of better things for you, and things that accompany salvation, even though we speak like this.

Kikuyu: Tondũ Ngai ndaagĩte kĩhooto; ndakaariganĩrwo nĩ wĩra wanyu o na wendo ũrĩa muonanĩtie nĩ ũndũ wa rĩĩtwa rĩake rĩrĩa mwateithagia andũ arĩa aamũre, o na rĩu no mũrathiĩ na mbere na kũmateithia.
English: For God is not unrighteous, so as to forget your work and the labor of love which you showed toward his name, in that you served the saints, and still do serve them.

Kikuyu: Tũngĩenda mũndũ o mũndũ wanyu onanie kĩyo o ta kĩu o nginya mũthia, nĩguo mũkaahingĩrio maũndũ marĩa mũtũire mwĩrĩgĩrĩire.
English: We desire that each one of you may show the same diligence to the fullness of hope even to the end,

Kikuyu: Tũtikwenda mũtuĩke igũũta, no tũkwenda mwĩgerekanagie na andũ, arĩa nĩ ũndũ wa gwĩtĩkia na gũkirĩrĩria kwao nĩkuo gũtũmaga magaĩrwo maũndũ marĩa meranĩirwo.
English: that you won’t be sluggish, but imitators of those who through faith and perseverance inherited the promises.

Kikuyu: Rĩrĩa Ngai eerĩire Iburahĩmu kĩĩranĩro gĩake, eehĩtire akĩĩgwetaga we mwene, nĩgũkorwo gũtiarĩ na ũngĩ mũnene kũrĩ we wa kwĩhĩta nake,
English: For when God made a promise to Abraham, since he could swear by no one greater, he swore by himself,

Kikuyu: akiuga atĩrĩ, “Ti-itherũ nĩngũkũrathima na ngũhe njiaro nyingĩ.”
English: saying, “Surely blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply you.”*

Kikuyu: Na nĩ ũndũ ũcio, thuutha wa Iburahĩmu gweterera akirĩrĩirie-rĩ, nĩaheirwo kĩrĩa eerĩirwo.
English: Thus, having patiently endured, he obtained the promise.

Kikuyu: Tondũ rĩĩrĩ, andũ mehĩtaga na mũndũ ũrĩa mũnene kũmakĩra, naguo mwĩhĩtwa ũgakindĩra ũrĩa kwĩrĩtwo, na ũgakĩniina ngarari ciothe.
English: For men indeed swear by a greater one, and in every dispute of theirs the oath is final for confirmation.

Kikuyu: Na tondũ Ngai nĩendaga kuonania hatarĩ nganja kũrĩ agai a maũndũ marĩa meranĩirwo atĩ itua rĩake rĩrĩa aatuĩte rĩtingĩgarũrũka-rĩ, nĩakindĩrire ũhoro ũcio na mwĩhĩtwa.
English: In this way God, being determined to show more abundantly to the heirs of the promise the immutability of his counsel, interposed with an oath,

Kikuyu: Ngai eekire ũguo na ũndũ wa maũndũ meerĩ matangĩgarũrĩka, o marĩa gũtangĩhoteka Ngai aheenanie namo, nĩgeetha ithuĩ arĩa tuonete handũ ha kũũrĩra twĩgwatĩre kĩĩrĩgĩrĩro kĩrĩa tũheetwo, tũhote kũũmĩrĩria mũno.
English: that by two immutable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we may have a strong encouragement, who have fled for refuge to take hold of the hope set before us.

Kikuyu: Kĩĩrĩgĩrĩro gĩkĩ tũrĩ nakĩo kĩhaana ta nanga ya ngoro, nakĩo nĩ kĩrũmu, na nĩ kĩa ma. Nakĩo gĩtoonyaga handũ-harĩa-haamũre thuutha wa gĩtama kĩrĩa kĩnene,
English: This hope we have as an anchor of the soul, a hope both sure and steadfast and entering into that which is within the veil,

Kikuyu: o harĩa Jesũ, ũrĩa wathiire mbere iitũ, aatoonyire ithenya riitũ. Nake nĩatuĩkĩte mũthĩnjĩri-Ngai ũrĩa mũnene o nginya tene, o ta ũrĩa Melikisedeki aatariĩ.
English: where as a forerunner Jesus entered for us, having become a high priest forever after the order of Melchizedek.

Kikuyu: Atĩrĩrĩ, Melikisedeki ũcio aarĩ mũthamaki wa Salemu na mũthĩnjĩri-Ngai, o Ngai-Ũrĩa-ũrĩ-Igũrũ- Mũno. Nĩwe watũngire Iburahĩmu akĩinũka aarĩkia kũhoota athamaki, na akĩmũrathima,
English: For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him,

Kikuyu: nake Iburahĩmu akĩmũhe gĩcunjĩ gĩa ikũmi kĩa indo ciothe. Rĩĩtwa rĩake rĩgĩtaũrwo mbere nĩ kuuga “mũthamaki wa ũthingu”; ningĩ “mũthamaki wa Salemu” nĩ kuuga “mũthamaki wa thayũ”.
English: to whom also Abraham divided a tenth part of all (being first, by interpretation, “king of righteousness”, and then also “king of Salem”, which means “king of peace”,

Kikuyu: Ndaarĩ na ithe kana nyina, kana kĩruka gĩake, na ndaarĩ na kĩambĩrĩria kĩa matukũ kana mũthia wa muoyo wake, nĩ ũndũ ũcio, we ahaana ta Mũrũ wa Ngai, egũtũũra arĩ mũthĩnjĩri-Ngai nginya tene.
English: without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but made like the Son of God), remains a priest continually.

Kikuyu: Ta mwĩciirie ũrĩa aarĩ mũnene: Atĩ o na ithe witũ Iburahĩmu nĩamũgaĩire gĩcunjĩ gĩa ikũmi kĩa indo iria aatahĩte!
English: Now consider how great this man was, to whom even Abraham the patriarch gave a tenth out of the best plunder.

Kikuyu: Na rĩrĩ, watho uugĩte atĩ andũ a rũciaro rwa Lawi arĩa matuĩkaga athĩnjĩri-Ngai metagie gĩcunjĩ gĩa ikũmi kuuma kũrĩ andũ, ũguo nĩ kuuga ariũ a ithe wao, o na gwatuĩka ariũ a ithe wao nĩ a rũciaro rwa Iburahĩmu.
English: They indeed of the sons of Levi who receive the priest’s office have a commandment to take tithes from the people according to the law, that is, of their brothers, though these have come out of the body of Abraham,

Kikuyu: No mũndũ ũcio ndaarĩ wa rũciaro rwa Lawi, no nĩamũkĩrire gĩcunjĩ gĩa ikũmi kuuma kũrĩ Iburahĩmu, na akĩrathima ũcio werĩirwo ciĩranĩro.
English: but he whose genealogy is not counted from them has accepted tithes from Abraham, and has blessed him who has the promises.

Kikuyu: Na hatirĩ nganja atĩ mũndũ ũrĩa mũnini nĩwe ũrathimagwo nĩ ũrĩa mũnene.
English: But without any dispute the lesser is blessed by the greater.

Kikuyu: Tũgakĩona atĩ, mwena ũmwe gĩcunjĩ kĩu gĩa ikũmi kĩũnganagio nĩ andũ arĩa macookaga gũkua, na nĩo Alawii; naguo mwena ũcio ũngĩ, kĩrutagĩrwo mũndũ ũrĩa uumbũrĩtwo ũhoro wake atĩ atũũraga o muoyo.
English: Here people who die receive tithes, but there one receives tithes of whom it is testified that he lives.

Kikuyu: O na mũndũ no oige atĩ Lawi, ũcio ũrutagĩrwo gĩcunjĩ kĩu gĩa ikũmi, we mwene nĩarutire gĩcunjĩ kĩu na njĩra ya Iburahĩmu,
English: We can say that through Abraham even Levi, who receives tithes, has paid tithes,

Kikuyu: tondũ hĩndĩ ĩrĩa Melikisedeki aacemanirie na Iburahĩmu, Lawi aarĩ mũthiimo-inĩ wa ithe ũcio wa tene.
English: for he was yet in the body of his father when Melchizedek met him.

Kikuyu: Korwo ũkinyanĩru kũna nĩũngĩonekanire na njĩra ya ũthĩnjĩri Ngai wa Alawii-rĩ, (nĩ ũndũ kĩrĩndĩ kĩaheirwo watho na njĩra ĩyo), gwakĩrĩ bata ũngĩ ũrĩkũ gũũke mũthĩnjĩri-Ngai ũngĩ, ũtariĩ ta Melikisedeki, na ndatuĩke ta wa nyũmba ya Harũni?
English: Now if perfection was through the Levitical priesthood (for under it the people have received the law), what further need was there for another priest to arise after the order of Melchizedek, and not be called after the order of Aaron?

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo ũhoro wa ũthĩnjĩri-Ngai ũngĩgarũrĩrwo-rĩ, o naguo watho no nginya ũgarũrĩrwo.
English: For the priesthood being changed, there is of necessity a change made also in the law.

Kikuyu: Nake mũndũ ũrĩa maũndũ maya maarĩtio nĩ ũndũ wake oimĩte mũhĩrĩga-inĩ ũngĩ, ũrĩa gũtarĩ mũndũ waguo ũrĩ watungatĩra Ngai kĩgongona- inĩ.
English: For he of whom these things are said belongs to another tribe, from which no one has officiated at the altar.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo nĩkũĩkaine wega atĩ Mwathani witũ oimire mũhĩrĩga-inĩ wa Juda, na ha ũhoro wa mũhĩrĩga ũcio-rĩ, Musa ndaigana kuuga ũndũ o na ũrĩkũ ũkoniĩ athĩnjĩri-Ngai.
English: For it is evident that our Lord has sprung out of Judah, about which tribe Moses spoke nothing concerning priesthood.

Kikuyu: Na rĩrĩ, ũhoro ũrĩa twarĩtie no ũmenyeke wega makĩria angĩkorwo mũthĩnjĩri-Ngai ũngĩ ũtariĩ ta Melikisedeki nĩonekanĩte,
English: This is yet more abundantly evident, if after the likeness of Melchizedek there arises another priest,

Kikuyu: ũrĩa ũtuĩkĩte mũthĩnjĩri-Ngai, na ti kũringana na mũtugo wa rũciaro rwake, no nĩ tondũ wa ũhoti wa muoyo ũrĩa ũtathiraga.
English: who has been made, not after the law of a fleshly commandment, but after the power of an endless life;

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo nĩkuumbũrĩtwo atĩrĩ: “Wee ũrĩ mũthĩnjĩri-Ngai nginya tene, o ta ũrĩa Melikisedeki aatariĩ.”
English: for it is testified, “You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek.”*

Kikuyu: Watho wa mbere nĩũtiganĩtwo naguo tondũ ndwarĩ na hinya na ũkaaga bata
English: For there is an annulling of a foregoing commandment because of its weakness and uselessness

Kikuyu: (nĩgũkorwo watho ndũrĩ ũndũ watũmire wagĩrĩre kũna), no nĩtũheetwo kĩĩrĩgĩrĩro kĩega makĩria kĩrĩa gĩtũhotithagia gũkuhĩrĩria Ngai.
English: (for the law made nothing perfect), and a bringing in of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.

Kikuyu: Na ũndũ ũyũ ndwekirwo hatarĩ mwĩhĩtwa! Andũ acio angĩ nĩmatuĩkaga athĩnjĩri-Ngai hatarĩ mwĩhĩtwa,
English: Inasmuch as he was not made priest without the taking of an oath

Kikuyu: nowe aatuĩkire mũthĩnjĩri-Ngai na mwĩhĩtwa, rĩrĩa Ngai aamwĩrire atĩrĩ: “Jehova nĩehĩtĩte, na ndangĩĩricũkwo, akoiga atĩrĩ: ‘Wee ũrĩ mũthĩnjĩri-Ngai nginya tene.’ ”
English: (for they indeed have been made priests without an oath), but he with an oath by him that says of him, “The Lord swore and will not change his mind, ‘You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek.’ ”*

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ wa mwĩhĩtwa ũyũ, Jesũ nĩatuĩkĩte mũrũgamĩrĩri wa kĩrĩkanĩro kĩrĩa kĩega makĩria.
English: By so much, Jesus has become the guarantee of a better covenant.

Kikuyu: Ningĩ-rĩ, nĩgũkoretwo na athĩnjĩri-Ngai aingĩ ta acio hau mbere, nĩgũkorwo nĩmakuaga magakĩgirio gũthiĩ na mbere na ũtungata ũcio.
English: Many, indeed, have been made priests, because they are hindered from continuing by death.

Kikuyu: No tondũ Jesũ atũũraga muoyo nginya tene-rĩ, ũthĩnjĩri-Ngai wake nĩ wa gũtũũra nginya tene.
English: But he, because he lives forever, has his priesthood unchangeable.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio nĩahotaga kũhonokia kũna arĩa othe mokaga kũrĩ Ngai magereire harĩ we, nĩgũkorwo egũtũũra amathaithanagĩrĩra.
English: Therefore he is also able to save to the uttermost those who draw near to God through him, seeing that he lives forever to make intercession for them.

Kikuyu: Tondũ nĩ kwagĩrĩire tũgĩe na mũthĩnjĩri-Ngai mũnene ta ũcio, atũhingagĩrie bata witũ, na akorwo arĩ mũtheru, na atarĩ ũcuuke, kana rĩhia, na aamũranĩtio na ehia, o na agatũũgĩrio igũrũ rĩa igũrũ.
English: For such a high priest was fitting for us: holy, guiltless, undefiled, separated from sinners, and made higher than the heavens;

Kikuyu: We ndekũbatara kũruta magongona mũthenya o mũthenya ta ũrĩa athĩnjĩri-Ngai anene acio angĩ meekaga, mbere nĩ ũndũ wa mehia make mwene, na thuutha ũcio nĩ ũndũ wa mehia ma kĩrĩndĩ. We nĩarutire igongona nĩ ũndũ wa mehia mao ihinda o rĩmwe rĩa kũigana hĩndĩ ĩrĩa eerutire we mwene.
English: who doesn’t need, like those high priests, to offer up sacrifices daily, first for his own sins, and then for the sins of the people. For he did this once for all, when he offered up himself.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo watho ũtuaga andũ matarĩ hinya athĩnjĩri Ngai anene; no mwĩhĩtwa, ũrĩa wokire thuutha wa watho, nĩwaamũrire Mũriũ, ũrĩa ũtuĩkĩte mwagĩrĩru kũna nginya tene.
English: For the law appoints men as high priests who have weakness, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son forever who has been perfected.

Kikuyu: Atĩrĩrĩ, ũhoro ũrĩa tũraaria nĩ atĩ: Nĩ tũrĩ na mũthĩnjĩri-Ngai-mũnene, ũrĩa ũikarĩte thĩ guoko-inĩ kwa ũrĩo gwa gĩtĩ kĩa Ũnene kĩa ũthamaki wa igũrũ,
English: Now in the things which we are saying, the main point is this: we have such a high priest, who sat down on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens,

Kikuyu: nake nĩ mũtungatĩri wa handũ-harĩa-haamũre, o kũu hema-inĩ ya gũtũnganwo ĩrĩa ya ma ĩrĩa yaakirwo nĩ Mwathani, no ti mũndũ.
English: a servant of the sanctuary and of the true tabernacle which the Lord pitched, not man.

Kikuyu: Na rĩrĩ, mũthĩnjĩri-Ngai mũnene o wothe aathuuragwo nĩguo arutage iheo na magongona, na nĩ ũndũ ũcio o nake no nginya akorwo arĩ na kĩndũ gĩa kũruta.
English: For every high priest is appointed to offer both gifts and sacrifices. Therefore it is necessary that this high priest also have something to offer.

Kikuyu: Korwo arĩ o gũkũ thĩ-rĩ, ndangĩrĩ mũthĩnjĩri-Ngai, nĩgũkorwo nĩ kũrĩ andũ arĩa marutaga iheo iria ciathanĩtwo nĩ watho.
English: For if he were on earth, he would not be a priest at all, seeing there are priests who offer the gifts according to the law,

Kikuyu: Nao matungataga mũhianĩre wa handũ-harĩa-haamũre na kĩĩruru kĩa maũndũ marĩa marĩ igũrũ. Ũndũ ũcio nĩguo watũmire Musa ataarwo hĩndĩ ĩrĩa eeharagĩria gwaka Hema-ya-Gũtũnganwo, akĩĩrwo atĩrĩ: “Menyerera wone nĩwathondeka indo icio ciothe kũringana na mũhianĩre ũrĩa wonirio ũrĩ kĩrĩma- inĩ.”
English: who serve a copy and shadow of the heavenly things, even as Moses was warned by God when he was about to make the tabernacle, for he said, “See, you shall make everything according to the pattern that was shown to you on the mountain.”*

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩ, ũtungata ũrĩa Jesũ aheetwo nĩũkĩrĩte wao, o ta ũrĩa kĩrĩkanĩro kĩrĩa arĩ we mũiguithania wakĩo gĩkĩrĩte kĩrĩa gĩkũrũ, na ningĩ kĩhaandĩtwo na ciĩranĩro njega makĩria.
English: But now he has obtained a more excellent ministry, by as much as he is also the mediator of a better covenant, which on better promises has been given as law.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo kĩrĩkanĩro kĩa mbere gĩtangĩarĩ na mahĩtia, gũtingĩagĩire bata wa gwetha kĩngĩ gĩa keerĩ.
English: For if that first covenant had been faultless, then no place would have been sought for a second.

Kikuyu: No Ngai nĩoonire andũ marĩ na mahĩtia, akiuga atĩrĩ: “Matukũ nĩmarooka, rĩrĩa ngaarĩkanĩra kĩrĩkanĩro kĩerũ na nyũmba ya Isiraeli, o hamwe na nyũmba ya Juda, nĩguo Mwathani ekuuga.
English: For finding fault with them, he said, “Behold,† the days are coming”, says the Lord, “that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah;

Kikuyu: Nakĩo kĩrĩkanĩro kĩu gĩtikahaana ta kĩrĩkanĩro kĩrĩa ndaarĩkanĩire na maithe mao ma tene rĩrĩa ndaamanyiitire na guoko, ngĩmatongoria, ngĩmaruta bũrũri wa Misiri, na tondũ matiigana gũikara marĩ ehokeku harĩ kĩrĩkanĩro gĩakwa, na niĩ ngĩmahutatĩra, ũguo nĩguo Mwathani ekuuga.
English: not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day that I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; for they didn’t continue in my covenant, and I disregarded them,” says the Lord.

Kikuyu: Gĩkĩ nĩkĩo kĩrĩkanĩro kĩrĩa ngaarĩkanĩra na nyũmba ya Isiraeli ihinda rĩu rĩathira, nĩguo Mwathani ekuuga. Nĩngekĩra watho wakwa meciiria-inĩ mao, na ningĩ ndĩwaandĩke ngoro-inĩ ciao. Na niĩ ngaatuĩka Ngai wao, nao matuĩke andũ akwa.
English: “For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days,” says the Lord: “I will put my laws into their mind; I will also write them on their heart. I will be their God, and they will be my people.

Kikuyu: Gũtigacooka gũkorwo na mũndũ ũkũruta ũrĩa ũngĩ, kana mũndũ arute mũrũ wa ithe amwĩre atĩrĩ, ‘Menyana na Mwathani,’ tondũ andũ othe nĩmagakorwo maamenyete, kuuma ũrĩa mũnini mũno wao nginya ũrĩa mũnene.
English: They will not teach every man his fellow citizen‡ and every man his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ for all will know me, from their least to their greatest.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo nĩngamarekera waganu wao, na ndigacooka kũririkana mehia mao.”
English: For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness. I will remember their sins and lawless deeds no more.”*

Kikuyu: Na rĩrĩ, rĩrĩa ekwaria ũhoro wa kĩrĩkanĩro kĩerũ-rĩ, nĩgũtua aatuire kĩrĩa kĩa mbere gĩkũrũ; na kĩndũ o gĩothe kĩrakũra-rĩ, gĩtuĩkaga gĩa gũthira, gĩkabuĩria o biũ.
English: In that he says, “A new covenant”, he has made the first obsolete. But that which is becoming obsolete and grows aged is near to vanishing away.

Kikuyu: Rĩu-rĩ, kĩrĩkanĩro kĩrĩa kĩa mbere nĩ kĩarĩ na mawatho maakoniĩ ũhoro wa kũhooya Ngai, o na ningĩ nĩ kwarĩ na handũ-harĩa-haamũre gũkũ thĩ.
English: Now indeed even the first† covenant had ordinances of divine service and an earthly sanctuary.

Kikuyu: Nĩ kwarĩ na hema yathondeketwo, na kanyũmba kayo ka mbere nĩ haarĩ na mũtĩ ũrĩa wa gũcuuria matawa, na metha, na mĩgate ĩrĩa mĩamũre; hau nĩho heetagwo “Handũ-harĩa-Hatheru.”
English: For a tabernacle was prepared. In the first part were the lamp stand, the table, and the show bread, which is called the Holy Place.

Kikuyu: Thuutha wa gĩtama gĩa keerĩ haarĩ na kanyũmba geetagwo, “Handũ-harĩa-Hatheru-Mũno,”
English: After the second veil was the tabernacle which is called the Holy of Holies,

Kikuyu: na hau nĩho haarĩ kĩgongona gĩa thahabu gĩa gũcinĩrwo ũbumba, na nĩho haarĩ ithandũkũ rĩa kĩrĩkanĩro rĩrĩa rĩahumbĩrĩtwo na thahabu kũndũ guothe. Thĩinĩ wa ithandũkũ rĩu nĩ haarĩ na nyũngũ ya thahabu yarĩ na mana, na rũthanju rwa Harũni rũrĩa rwathundũkĩte, na ihengere cia mahiga iria ciandĩkĩtwo.
English: having a golden altar of incense and the ark of the covenant overlaid on all sides with gold, in which was a golden pot holding the manna, Aaron’s rod that budded, and the tablets of the covenant;

Kikuyu: Igũrũ wa ithandũkũ rĩu nĩ haarĩ na akerubi a Riiri, mahumbĩrĩte gĩtĩ-gĩa-tha. No rĩu tũtingĩhota gũtaarĩria wega rĩu ũhoro wa kĩndũ o kĩndũ.
English: and above it cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat, of which things we can’t speak now in detail.

Kikuyu: Nacio indo ciothe ciarĩkia kũbangwo ũguo-rĩ, athĩnjĩri-Ngai nao maatoonyaga kanyũmba kau ka mbere hĩndĩ ciothe nĩguo marute wĩra wao wa ũtungata.
English: Now these things having been thus prepared, the priests go in continually into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the services,

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩ, mũthĩnjĩri-Ngai ũrĩa mũnene nowe wiki watoonyaga kanyũmba karĩa ga thĩinĩ, na aatoonyaga o ihinda o rĩmwe mwaka, na ndangĩatoonyire atakuuĩte thakame ya kũruta igongona nĩ ũndũ wake mwene na nĩ ũndũ wa mehia ma andũ marĩa meekĩte matekũmenya.
English: but into the second the high priest alone, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the errors of the people.

Kikuyu: Ũndũ ũyũ nĩguo Roho Mũtheru oonanagia naguo atĩ njĩra ya gũtoonya Handũ-harĩa-Hatheru-Mũno ndĩakoretwo ĩguũranĩirio ihinda rĩrĩa rĩothe hema ya mbere yarĩ ho.
English: The Holy Spirit is indicating this, that the way into the Holy Place wasn’t yet revealed while the first tabernacle was still standing.

Kikuyu: Gĩkĩ gĩkĩrĩ o kĩonereria kĩa matukũ maya tũrĩ, atĩ maruta na magongona marĩa maarutagwo matingĩahotire gũtheria thamiri ya mũndũ ũrĩa mũhooi Ngai.
English: This is a symbol of the present age, where gifts and sacrifices are offered that are incapable, concerning the conscience, of making the worshiper perfect,

Kikuyu: Maũndũ macio makoniĩ o ũhoro wa kũrĩa na kũnyua, na magongona ma mĩthemba mĩingĩ ya gwĩtheria na mawatho ma na igũrũ tu, marĩa maathanĩtwo mekagwo nginya ihinda rĩrĩa maũndũ makeerũhio rĩgaakinya.
English: being only (with foods and drinks and various washings) fleshly ordinances, imposed until a time of reformation.

Kikuyu: Rĩrĩa Kristũ ookire arĩ mũthĩnjĩri-Ngai ũrĩa mũnene wa maũndũ mega marĩa marĩ kuo-rĩ, nĩagereire hema-inĩ ĩrĩa nene na nginyanĩru ĩrĩa ĩtathondeketwo na moko ma andũ, naguo ũguo nĩ kuuga ti ya mũmbĩre wa thĩ ĩno.
English: But Christ having come as a high priest of the coming good things, through the greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this creation,

Kikuyu: Ndaatoonyire na ũndũ wa thakame ya mbũri na njaũ; nowe aatoonyire Handũ-harĩa-Hatheru-Mũno riita o rĩmwe rĩa kũigana na ũndũ wa thakame yake we mwene, arĩkĩtie gũkũũra andũ na ũkũũri ũrĩa ũtagaathira.
English: nor yet through the blood of goats and calves, but through his own blood, entered in once for all into the Holy Place, having obtained eternal redemption.

Kikuyu: Thakame ya mbũri na ndegwa, na mũhu wa moori ĩcinĩtwo, ciaminjaminjĩrio arĩa marĩ na thaahu, nĩciamatheragia na ikaniina thaahu mĩĩrĩ yao.
English: For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkling those who have been defiled, sanctify to the cleanness of the flesh,

Kikuyu: Githĩ thakame ya Kristũ, ũrĩa werutire arĩ igongona rĩtarĩ kaũũgũ harĩ Ngai nĩ ũndũ wa Roho wa tene na tene, ndĩngĩgĩtheria thamiri ciitũ makĩria nĩguo itigane na ciĩko iria cierekagĩria mũndũ gĩkuũ-inĩ, nĩguo tũtungatagĩre Ngai ũrĩa ũtũũraga muoyo!
English: how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without defect to God, cleanse your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio-rĩ, Kristũ nĩwe mũiguithania wa kĩrĩkanĩro kĩerũ, nĩguo arĩa metĩtwo mahote kũgaĩrwo igai rĩrĩa rĩĩranĩirwo rĩtagaathira, kuona atĩ rĩu nĩakuĩte arĩ mũkũũri wa kũmakũũra kuuma mehia-inĩ marĩa meekĩtwo kĩrĩkanĩro-inĩ kĩrĩa kĩa mbere.
English: For this reason he is the mediator of a new covenant, since a death has occurred for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first covenant, that those who have been called may receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.

Kikuyu: Tondũ ha ũhoro ũkoniĩ kwĩgaya-rĩ, nĩ kwagĩrĩire kũmenyeke wega atĩ ũcio wĩgaĩte nĩakuĩte,
English: For where a last will and testament is, there must of necessity be the death of him who made it.

Kikuyu: nĩ ũndũ kwĩgaya kũgĩaga na hinya rĩrĩa mũndũ ũrĩa wĩgaĩte aarĩkia gũkua; kwĩgaya gũtirĩ hinya rĩrĩa rĩothe ũrĩa wĩgaĩte arĩ muoyo.
English: For a will is in force where there has been death, for it is never in force while he who made it lives.

Kikuyu: Ũguo noguo o nakĩo kĩrĩkanĩro kĩa mbere gĩtingĩagĩire na hinya hatarĩ thakame.
English: Therefore even the first covenant has not been dedicated without blood.

Kikuyu: Hĩndĩ ĩrĩa Musa aarĩkirie kũhe andũ othe maathani mothe marĩa maandĩkĩtwo watho-inĩ-rĩ, nĩoire thakame ya njaũ, o hamwe na maaĩ, na guoya mũtune, na mathĩgĩ ma mũthobi akĩminjaminjĩria ibuku rĩa gĩkũnjo o na andũ othe.
English: For when every commandment had been spoken by Moses to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of the calves and the goats, with water and scarlet wool and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book itself and all the people,

Kikuyu: Akĩmeera atĩrĩ, “Ĩno nĩyo thakame ya kĩrĩkanĩro, kĩrĩa Ngai amwathĩte mwathĩkagĩre.”
English: saying, “This is the blood of the covenant which God has commanded you.”*

Kikuyu: Ningĩ o ũndũ ũmwe, akĩminjaminjĩria Hema-ya-Gũtũnganwo thakame o hamwe na indo iria ciothe ciahũthagĩrwo gũtungatĩra Ngai nacio.
English: He sprinkled the tabernacle and all the vessels of the ministry in the same way with the blood.

Kikuyu: Na ti-itherũ, kũringana na watho hakuhĩ indo ciothe itheragio na thakame, na hatarĩ gũitwo gwa thakame-rĩ, gũtirĩ kũrekerwo kwa mehia.
English: According to the law, nearly everything is cleansed with blood, and apart from shedding of blood there is no remission.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio, nĩ kwagĩrĩire mĩhaano ya indo iria irĩ igũrũ ĩtheragio na magongona macio, no indo cia igũrũ cio nyene itheragio na magongona mega kũrĩ macio.
English: It was necessary therefore that the copies of the things in the heavens should be cleansed with these, but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo Kristũ ndaatoonyire handũ-harĩa-haamũre haakĩtwo na moko ma andũ hahaanaine na handũ harĩa ha ma; nowe aatoonyire igũrũ kuo kwene, kũrĩa rĩu arũgamĩte mbere ya Ngai nĩ ũndũ witũ.
English: For Christ hasn’t entered into holy places made with hands, which are representations of the true, but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us;

Kikuyu: O na ndaatoonyire igũrũ nĩguo erutage igongona kaingĩ kaingĩ ta ũrĩa mũthĩnjĩri-Ngai mũnene aatoonyaga Handũ-harĩa-Hatheru-Mũno o mwaka arĩ na thakame ĩtarĩ yake mwene.
English: nor yet that he should offer himself often, as the high priest enters into the holy place year by year with blood not his own,

Kikuyu: Kũngĩrĩ ũguo-rĩ, Kristũ angĩtũũraga anyariiragwo kuuma rĩrĩa thĩ yombirwo. No rĩu, matukũ-inĩ maya ma kũrigĩrĩria, nĩaguũranĩirio riita rĩmwe rĩa kũigana nĩguo eherie wĩhia na ũndũ wa kwĩruta atuĩke igongona we mwene.
English: or else he must have suffered often since the foundation of the world. But now once at the end of the ages, he has been revealed to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.

Kikuyu: Na o ta ũrĩa gũtuĩtwo atĩ andũ makuage o riita rĩmwe, na thuutha wa ũguo magatuĩrwo ciira-rĩ,
English: Inasmuch as it is appointed for men to die once, and after this, judgment,

Kikuyu: ũguo no taguo Kristũ aarutirwo igongona riita o rĩmwe nĩguo eherie mehia ma andũ aingĩ; nake nĩakaguũranĩrio riita rĩa keerĩ, no tigeetha akuue mehia, no nĩgeetha arehere arĩa mamwetagĩrĩra ũhonokio.
English: so Christ also, having been offered once to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time, not to deal with sin, but to save those who are eagerly waiting for him.

Kikuyu: Rĩu-rĩ, watho no kĩĩruru kĩa maũndũ mega marĩa magooka, no ti mũhianĩre wa maũndũ marĩa mo mene. Nĩ ũndũ ũcio watho ndũngĩhota gũtũma magongona marĩa marutagwo o mwaka o mwaka mategũtigithĩrio matũme andũ arĩa mookaga kũhooya Ngai magĩrĩre kũna.
English: For the law, having a shadow of the good to come, not the very image of the things, can never with the same sacrifices year by year, which they offer continually, make perfect those who draw near.

Kikuyu: Tondũ korwo nĩ kwahotekire-rĩ, githĩ magongona macio matingĩagĩtigire kũrutagwo? Nĩgũkorwo arĩa maahooyaga nĩmangĩatheretio rĩmwe rĩa kũigana, na matingĩacookire gwĩcuukĩra mehia mao.
English: Or else wouldn’t they have ceased to be offered, because the worshipers, having been once cleansed, would have had no more consciousness of sins?

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩ, magongona macio maarĩ ma kũririkanania mehia mwaka o mwaka,
English: But in those sacrifices there is a yearly reminder of sins.

Kikuyu: tondũ gũtingĩhoteka thakame ya ndegwa na ya mbũri yeherie mehia.
English: For it is impossible that the blood of bulls and goats should take away sins.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio, hĩndĩ ĩrĩa Kristũ ookire gũkũ thĩ, oigire atĩrĩ: “Wee ti magongona na maruta weriragĩria, no nĩ mwĩrĩ wahaarĩrĩirie;
English: Therefore when he comes into the world, he says, “You didn’t desire sacrifice and offering, but you prepared a body for me.

Kikuyu: ndwakenirio nĩ maruta ma njino, o na kana maruta ma kũhoroheria mehia.
English: You had no pleasure in whole burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin.

Kikuyu: Hĩndĩ ĩyo ngiuga atĩrĩ, ‘Niĩ ũyũ haha, o ta ũrĩa ũhoro wakwa wandĩkĩtwo ibuku-inĩ rĩa gĩkũnjo, atĩrĩ: njũkĩte gwĩka wendi waku, Wee Ngai.’ ”
English: Then I said, ‘Behold, I have come (in the scroll of the book it is written of me) to do your will, O God.’ ”*

Kikuyu: Mbere oigire atĩrĩ, “Magongona na maruta, na maruta ma njino, o na maruta ma kũhoroherio mehia, ti mo weriragĩria, o na kana ũgakenio nĩmo” (o na gũtuĩka watho nĩwaathanĩte marutagwo).
English: Previously saying, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin you didn’t desire, neither had pleasure in them” (those which are offered according to the law),

Kikuyu: Ningĩ akiuga atĩrĩ, “Niĩ ũyũ haha, njũkĩte gwĩka wendi waku.” Eeheragia ũhoro wa mbere nĩguo ahaande ũcio wa keerĩ.
English: then he has said, “Behold, I have come to do your will.” He takes away the first, that he may establish the second,

Kikuyu: Na nĩ ũndũ wa kwenda kũu-rĩ, nĩtũtuĩtwo atheru nĩ ũndũ wa igongona rĩa mwĩrĩ wa Jesũ Kristũ rĩrĩa aarutire ihinda rĩmwe rĩa kũigana.
English: by which will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.

Kikuyu: Mũthenya o mũthenya mũthĩnjĩri-Ngai o wothe arũgamaga na akaruta mawĩra make makoniĩ kĩrĩra kĩa Ngai, agakĩruta magongona o ro macio kaingĩ kaingĩ, no nĩ magongona matangĩhota kweheria mehia.
English: Every priest indeed stands day by day serving and offering often the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins,

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩ, mũthĩnjĩri Ngai ũyũ aarĩkia kũruta igongona rĩmwe rĩa kũigana rĩa kweheria mehia, nĩaikarire thĩ guoko-inĩ kwa ũrĩo kwa Ngai.
English: but he, when he had offered one sacrifice for sins forever, sat down on the right hand of God,

Kikuyu: Kuuma hĩndĩ ĩyo nĩatũũraga etereire o nginya rĩrĩa thũ ciake igaatuuo gaturwa ka makinya make,
English: from that time waiting until his enemies are made the footstool of his feet.

Kikuyu: nĩ tondũ na ũndũ wa igongona rĩu rĩmwe, nĩatũmĩte arĩa maratuuo atheru magĩrĩre kũna nginya tene.
English: For by one offering he has perfected forever those who are being sanctified.

Kikuyu: O nake Roho Mũtheru nĩatumbũragĩra ũhoro ũyũ. O mbere akoiga atĩrĩ:
English: The Holy Spirit also testifies to us, for after saying,

Kikuyu: “Gĩkĩ nĩkĩo kĩrĩkanĩro kĩrĩa ngaarĩkanĩra nao thuutha wa matukũ macio, ũguo nĩguo Mwathani ekuuga. Nĩngekĩra mawatho makwa ngoro-inĩ ciao, na ndĩmaandĩke meciiria-inĩ mao.”
English: “This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days,” says the Lord, “I will put my laws on their heart, I will also write them on their mind;”* then he says,

Kikuyu: Ningĩ agacooka akoiga atĩrĩ: “Ndigacooka kũririkana mehia mao na ciĩko ciao cia ũremi o rĩ o rĩ.”
English: “I will remember their sins and their iniquities no more.”*

Kikuyu: Na rĩrĩ, mehia marĩkia kũrekanĩrwo-rĩ, gũtingĩcooka kũrutwo igongona rĩngĩ rĩa kweheria mehia.
English: Now where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio, ariũ na aarĩ a Ithe witũ, kuona atĩ tũrĩ na mwĩhoko wa gũtoonya Handũ-harĩa- Hatheru-Mũno, na ũndũ wa thakame ya Jesũ,
English: Having therefore, brothers, boldness to enter into the holy place by the blood of Jesus,

Kikuyu: tondũ nĩatũhingũrĩire njĩra njerũ na ĩrĩ muoyo ya kũhĩtũkĩra gĩtambaya-inĩ, nakĩo nĩkĩo mwĩrĩ wake,
English: by the way which he dedicated for us, a new and living way, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh,

Kikuyu: na kuona atĩ nĩ tũrĩ na mũthĩnjĩri-Ngai mũnene mũno ũrĩa ũrũgamĩrĩire nyũmba ya Ngai-rĩ,
English: and having a great priest over God’s house,

Kikuyu: nĩtũkuhĩrĩrie Ngai tũrĩ na ngoro itarĩ na ũhinga, na tũiyũrĩtwo nĩ wĩtĩkio kũna, nacio ngoro ciitũ iminjaminjĩirio nĩguo tũtherio thamiri ciitũ ciage ũcuuke nayo mĩĩrĩ iitũ ĩthambĩtio na maaĩ matheru.
English: let’s draw near with a true heart in fullness of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience and having our body washed with pure water,

Kikuyu: Ningĩ nĩtũrũmiei ũhoro wa kĩĩrĩgĩrĩro kĩrĩa tuumbũraga tũtegũthangania, nĩgũkorwo ũrĩa wĩranĩire kĩĩranĩro kĩu nĩ mwĩhokeku.
English: let’s hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering; for he who promised is faithful.

Kikuyu: Hamwe na ũguo, nĩtwĩcũũranie ũrĩa tũngĩarahũrana o mũndũ na ũrĩa ũngĩ ũhoro-inĩ wa kwendana na gwĩka ciĩko njega.
English: Let’s consider how to provoke one another to love and good works,

Kikuyu: Na ningĩ tũtigatige kũnganaga hamwe, ta ũrĩa andũ amwe mamenyerete gwĩkaga, no nĩtũmanagĩrĩriei mũndũ na ũrĩa ũngĩ, na makĩria mũno tondũ wa ũrĩa mũkuona atĩ Mũthenya ũcio nĩũrakuhĩrĩria.
English: not forsaking our own assembling together, as the custom of some is, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching.

Kikuyu: Tondũ tũngĩthiĩ na mbere na kwĩhia na ũtũrĩka thuutha wa kũmenya ũhoro-ũrĩa-wa-ma-rĩ, gũtirĩ na igongona rĩngĩ rĩa kweheria mehia rĩtigaire,
English: For if we sin willfully after we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remains no more a sacrifice for sins,

Kikuyu: tiga o gweterera tũrĩ na guoya ciira o na mwaki ũrĩrĩmbũkaga ũrĩa ũkaaniina thũ cia Ngai.
English: but a certain fearful expectation of judgment, and a fierceness of fire which will devour the adversaries.

Kikuyu: Mũndũ ũrĩa wothe wareganaga na watho wa Musa ooragagwo atekũiguĩrwo tha na ũndũ wa ũira wa andũ eerĩ kana atatũ.
English: A man who disregards Moses’ law dies without compassion on the word of two or three witnesses.

Kikuyu: Mũgwĩciiria mũndũ aagĩrĩirwo nĩkũherithio mũno makĩria atĩa, ũrĩa ũrangĩrĩirie Mũrũ wa Ngai thĩ, na agatua atĩ thakame ya kĩrĩkanĩro ĩrĩa aatheretio nayo ti theru, na agacooka akaruma Roho ũrĩa ũheanaga wega wa Ngai?
English: How much worse punishment do you think he will be judged worthy of who has trodden under foot the Son of God, and has counted the blood of the covenant with which he was sanctified an unholy thing, and has insulted the Spirit of grace?

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo nĩtũũĩ ũrĩa woigire atĩrĩ, “Kũrĩhanĩria nĩ gwakwa, na nĩ niĩ ngaarĩhanĩria,” na ningĩ akiuga atĩrĩ, “Mwathani nĩwe ũgaatuĩra andũ ake ciira.”
English: For we know him who said, “Vengeance belongs to me. I will repay,” says the Lord.* Again, “The Lord will judge his people.”*

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ wa kũguoyohia mũno mũndũ gũkumbatwo nĩ Ngai ũrĩa ũrĩ muoyo.
English: It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.

Kikuyu: Ririkanai matukũ ma tene thuutha wanyu kwarĩrwo nĩ ũtheri, ũrĩa mweyũmĩrĩirie mbaara nene rĩrĩa mwanyariiragwo.
English: But remember the former days, in which, after you were enlightened, you endured a great struggle with sufferings:

Kikuyu: Mahinda mamwe mwathĩĩnagio mbere ya kĩrĩndĩ mũkĩrumagwo; na mahinda mangĩ nĩmwanyiitanagĩra na arĩa meekagwo ũguo.
English: partly, being exposed to both reproaches and oppressions, and partly, becoming partakers with those who were treated so.

Kikuyu: Ningĩ nĩmwaiguagĩra arĩa mohetwo njeera tha, na mũgetĩkagĩra gũtunywo indo cianyu mũkenete, tondũ nĩmwamenyete atĩ inyuĩ mwarĩ na ũtonga ũngĩ mwega makĩria na wa gũtũũra.
English: For you both had compassion on me in my chains and joyfully accepted the plundering of your possessions, knowing that you have for yourselves a better possession and an enduring one in the heavens.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio, mũtigate ũũmĩrĩru ũcio wanyu; nĩgũkorwo nĩũkamũrehere uumithio mũnene.
English: Therefore don’t throw away your boldness, which has a great reward.

Kikuyu: Mwagĩrĩirwo nĩgũkirĩrĩria, nĩguo mwarĩkia gwĩka ũrĩa Ngai endaga, mũkaamũkĩra kĩrĩa eeranĩire.
English: For you need endurance so that, having done the will of God, you may receive the promise.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo kahinda kanini gaathira-rĩ, “Ũrĩa ũroka nĩegũka, na ndegũtĩĩra.
English: “In a very little while, he who comes will come and will not wait.

Kikuyu: No mũndũ wakwa ũrĩa mũthingu agaatũũra muoyo nĩ ũndũ wa gwĩtĩkia. Na angĩgacooka na thuutha, ngoro yakwa ndĩgakenio nĩwe.”
English: But the righteous one will live by faith. If he shrinks back, my soul has no pleasure in him.”*

Kikuyu: No ithuĩ tũtirĩ a thiritũ ya arĩa macookaga na thuutha makora, no tũrĩ a thiritũ ya arĩa metĩkagia, makahonokio.
English: But we are not of those who shrink back to destruction, but of those who have faith to the saving of the soul.

Kikuyu: Rĩu-rĩ, gwĩtĩkia nĩkũgĩa na ma ya maũndũ marĩa twĩrĩgĩrĩire, na kũmenya na ma atĩ maũndũ marĩa tũtonaga marĩ ho.
English: Now faith is assurance of things hoped for, proof of things not seen.

Kikuyu: Ũndũ ũcio nĩguo watũmire andũ arĩa maarĩ kuo tene magaathĩrĩrio.
English: For by this, the elders obtained approval.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ wa gwĩtĩkia-rĩ, nĩtũmenyaga atĩ thĩ yothe yombirwo na kiugo kĩa Ngai, na nĩ ũndũ ũcio indo iria cionagwo itiathondekirwo kuuma kũrĩ indo iria cionekanaga.
English: By faith we understand that the universe has been framed by the word of God, so that what is seen has not been made out of things which are visible.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ wa gwĩtĩkia-rĩ, Habili nĩarutĩire Ngai igongona rĩega gũkĩra rĩa Kaini. Na nĩ ũndũ wa gwĩtĩkia nĩagathĩrĩirio ta mũndũ mũthingu rĩrĩa Ngai aaheanire ũira mwega nĩ gwĩtĩkĩra maruta make. Na nĩ ũndũ wa gwĩtĩkia o na rĩu no aaragia o na gũtuĩka nĩakuire.
English: By faith Abel offered to God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, through which he had testimony given to him that he was righteous, God testifying with respect to his gifts; and through it he, being dead, still speaks.

Kikuyu: Na ũndũ wa gwĩtĩkia-rĩ, Enoku nĩeheririo mũtũũrĩre-inĩ ũyũ, nĩguo ndagacame gĩkuũ; na ndacookire kuonwo tondũ Ngai nĩamweheririe. Nĩgũkorwo ataneherio, nĩagathĩrĩirio atĩ aarĩ mũndũ wakenagia Ngai.
English: By faith Enoch was taken away, so that he wouldn’t see death, and he was not found, because God translated him. For he has had testimony given to him that before his translation he had been well pleasing to God.

Kikuyu: Na rĩrĩ, gũtarĩ na wĩtĩkio gũtingĩhoteka gũkenia Ngai, tondũ mũndũ ũrĩa wothe ũũkaga harĩ we no nginya etĩkie atĩ nĩ kũrĩ Ngai, na atĩ nĩwe ũheaga arĩa othe mamũcaragia na kĩyo iheo ciao.
English: Without faith it is impossible to be well pleasing to him, for he who comes to God must believe that he exists, and that he is a rewarder of those who seek him.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ wa gwĩtĩkia-rĩ, hĩndĩ ĩrĩa Nuhu aamenyithirio ũhoro wa maũndũ marĩa matoonekete-rĩ, nĩaakire thabina arĩ na wĩtigiri wa ngoro nĩguo ahonokie andũ a nyũmba yake. Nĩ ũndũ wa gwĩtĩkia gwake nĩatuĩrĩire thĩ ciira, na agĩtuĩka mũgai wa ũthingu ũrĩa uumanaga na gwĩtĩkia.
English: By faith Noah, being warned about things not yet seen, moved with godly fear,† prepared a ship for the saving of his house, through which he condemned the world and became heir of the righteousness which is according to faith.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ wa gwĩtĩkia-rĩ, Iburahĩmu rĩrĩa eetirwo athiĩ bũrũri ũrĩa aaheagwo ũtuĩke igai rĩake, nĩathĩkire na agĩthiĩ, o na akorwo ndaamenyaga kũrĩa aathiiaga.
English: By faith Abraham, when he was called, obeyed to go out to the place which he was to receive for an inheritance. He went out, not knowing where he went.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ wa gwĩtĩkia-rĩ, agĩtuĩka mũtũũri bũrũri-inĩwa kĩĩranĩroahaanata mũgenibũrũri-inĩwene; aatũũragahema-inĩ, o ũndũũmwe na Isaaka na Jakubu, arĩa maarĩ agai a kĩĩranĩro kĩu hamwe nake.
English: By faith he lived as an alien in the land of promise, as in a land not his own, dwelling in tents with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo nĩataanyaga kuona itũũra rĩrĩ na mĩthingi mĩrũmu, rĩrĩa mũthondeki na mwaki warĩo nĩ Ngai.
English: For he was looking for the city which has foundations, whose builder and maker is God.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ wa gwĩtĩkia-rĩ, Iburahĩmu, o na gũtuĩka nĩatindĩkĩte matukũ, nake Sara aarĩ thaata, nĩahotithirio gũtuĩka ithe wa mwana tondũ nĩatuĩte atĩ Ũrĩa weranĩire kĩĩranĩro kĩu aarĩ mwĩhokeku.
English: By faith even Sarah herself received power to conceive, and she bore a child when she was past age, since she counted him faithful who had promised.

Kikuyu: Na nĩ ũndũ ũcio kuuma harĩ mũndũ ũyũ ũmwe, o na aarĩ ta mũndũ mũkuũ-rĩ, gũgĩciarwo njiaro nyingĩ o ta njata cia igũrũ, o na ta mũthanga ũrĩa ũtangĩtarĩka ũrĩ hũgũrũrũ-inĩ cia iria.
English: Therefore as many as the stars of the sky in multitude, and as innumerable as the sand which is by the sea shore, were fathered by one man, and him as good as dead.

Kikuyu: Andũ aya othe maatũũrire marũmĩtie wĩtĩkio nginya rĩrĩa maakuire. Matiigana kũhingĩrio maũndũ marĩa meerĩirwo; no nĩmamonaga marĩ o kũraya na makamakenera. Nao nĩmoimbũraga atĩ o nĩ ageni na agendi gũkũ thĩ.
English: These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen‡ them and embraced them from afar, and having confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.

Kikuyu: Andũ arĩa moigaga maũndũ ta macio monanagia atĩ nĩ gwetha methaga bũrũri ũrĩa ũrĩ wao kĩũmbe.
English: For those who say such things make it clear that they are seeking a country of their own.

Kikuyu: Korwo nĩmeeciiragia ũhoro wa bũrũri ũrĩa moimĩte-rĩ, nĩ mangĩagĩte na mweke wa gũcooka kuo.
English: If indeed they had been thinking of that country from which they went out, they would have had enough time to return.

Kikuyu: Handũ ha ũguo, o meeriragĩria bũrũri mwega kũrĩ ũcio, naguo nĩ bũrũri wa igũrũ. Nĩ ũndũ ũcio Ngai ndaconokaga gwĩtwo Ngai wao, nĩgũkorwo nĩahaarĩirie itũũra inene nĩ ũndũ wao.
English: But now they desire a better country, that is, a heavenly one. Therefore God is not ashamed of them, to be called their God, for he has prepared a city for them.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ wa gwĩtĩkia-rĩ, Iburahĩmu, rĩrĩa aageririo nĩ Ngai, nĩarutire Isaaka atuĩke igongona. Ũcio werĩirwo ciĩranĩro nĩehaarĩirie kũruta mũrũ wake wa mũmwe igongona,
English: By faith, Abraham, being tested, offered up Isaac. Yes, he who had gladly received the promises was offering up his only born§ son,

Kikuyu: o na gũtuĩka Ngai nĩamwĩrĩte atĩrĩ, “Rũciaro rũrĩa rũgeetanio nawe rũkoima harĩ Isaaka.”
English: to whom it was said, “Your offspring will be accounted as from Isaac,” *

Kikuyu: Iburahĩmu nĩatuĩte na ngoro atĩ Ngai no ariũkie mũndũ mũkuũ, na nĩ ũndũ ũcio no kwĩrwo na ngerekano atĩ nĩacookeirio Isaaka ta oimĩte kũrĩ arĩa akuũ.
English: concluding that God is able to raise up even from the dead. Figuratively speaking, he also did receive him back from the dead.

Kikuyu: Na ũndũ wa gwĩtĩkia-rĩ, Isaaka nĩarathimire Jakubu na Esaũ akĩratha ũhoro wa matukũ mao ma thuutha.
English: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau, even concerning things to come.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ wa gwĩtĩkia-rĩ, Jakubu, rĩrĩa aarĩ hakuhĩ gũkua, nĩarathimire ariũ a Jusufu, o mũndũ riita rĩake, na akĩhooya Ngai enyiitĩrĩire mũthĩgi wake.
English: By faith Jacob, when he was dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph, and worshiped, leaning on the top of his staff.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ wa gwĩtĩkia-rĩ, Jusufu, nake, ihinda rĩake rĩa mũthia rĩakuhĩrĩria, nĩaririe ũhoro wa gũthaama kwa andũ a Isiraeli kuuma bũrũri wa Misiri, na agĩathana ũhoro ũkoniĩ mahĩndĩ make.
English: By faith Joseph, when his end was near, made mention of the departure of the children of Israel, and gave instructions concerning his bones.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ wa gwĩtĩkia-rĩ, aciari a Musa nĩmamũhithire ihinda rĩa mĩeri ĩtatũ kuuma aaciarwo tondũ nĩmoonire aarĩ mwana mwega, na matietigĩrire watho wa mũthamaki.
English: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hidden for three months by his parents, because they saw that he was a beautiful child; and they were not afraid of the king’s commandment.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ wa gwĩtĩkia-rĩ, Musa rĩrĩa aatuĩkire mũndũ mũgima nĩaregire gwĩtwo mũrũ wa mwarĩ wa Firaũni.
English: By faith Moses, when he had grown up, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter,

Kikuyu: Nĩathuurire kũnyariiranĩrio hamwe na andũ a Ngai, handũ ha gwĩkenia na mĩago ya wĩhia ya ihinda inini.
English: choosing rather to share ill treatment with God’s people than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a time,

Kikuyu: We nĩatuire atĩ kũmenwo nĩ ũndũ wa Kristũ nĩ uumithio mũnene gũkĩra ũtonga wa Misiri, nĩ tondũ nĩacũthagĩrĩria gũkaaheo kĩheo.
English: considering the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures of Egypt; for he looked to the reward.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ wa gwĩtĩkia-rĩ, nĩoimire Misiri ategwĩtigĩra marakara ma mũthamaki; nĩakirĩrĩirie tondũ nĩoonire Ũrĩa ũtonekaga.
English: By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king; for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ wa gwĩtĩkia-rĩ, nĩarũmirie gĩathĩ kĩa Bathaka na ũhoro wa kũminjaminjanĩrio gwa thakame, nĩguo mwanangi wa marigithathi ndakae kũhutia marigithathi ma andũ a Isiraeli.
English: By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of the blood, that the destroyer of the firstborn should not touch them.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ wa gwĩtĩkia-rĩ, andũ nĩmatuĩkanĩirie Iria Itune taarĩ thĩ nyũmũ maagereire; no rĩrĩa andũ a Misiri maageririe gwĩka ũguo, makĩrindanio nĩ maaĩ.
English: By faith they passed through the Red Sea as on dry land. When the Egyptians tried to do so, they were swallowed up.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ wa gwĩtĩkia-rĩ, thingo cia Jeriko nĩciagũire andũ maarĩkia gũcithiũrũrũka matukũ mũgwanja.
English: By faith the walls of Jericho fell down after they had been encircled for seven days.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ wa gwĩtĩkia-rĩ, mũmaraya ũrĩa wetagwo Rahabu, tondũ wa kũnyiita athigaani ũgeni, ndoraganĩirio na andũ arĩa maarĩ aremi.
English: By faith Rahab the prostitute didn’t perish with those who were disobedient, having received the spies in peace.

Kikuyu: Ingiuga atĩa ũngĩ? Ndirĩ na ihinda rĩa kũheana ũhoro wa Gideoni, na wa Baraka, na wa Samusoni, na wa Jefitha, na wa Daudi, na wa Samũeli, o na wa anabii,
English: What more shall I say? For the time would fail me if I told of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets—

Kikuyu: acio othe nĩ ũndũ wa gwĩtĩkia-rĩ, nĩmatooririe mothamaki, na magĩĩka maũndũ ma kĩhooto, na makĩĩgwatĩra kĩrĩa kĩeranĩirwo; nao makĩhinga mĩrũũthi tũnua,
English: who through faith subdued kingdoms, worked out righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions,*

Kikuyu: na makĩhoria mwaki warĩrĩmbũkaga, na makĩhonokio matikaniinwo na rũhiũ rwa njora; ũhinyaru wao wagarũrirwo ũgĩtuĩka hinya; ningĩ maarũire na ũcamba mbaara- inĩ na magĩtooria mbũtũ cia ita cia ndũrĩrĩ ingĩ.
English: quenched the power of fire,* escaped the edge of the sword,* from weakness were made strong, grew mighty in war, and caused foreign armies to flee.

Kikuyu: Nao andũ-a-nja makĩriũkĩrio andũ ao arĩa maakuĩte, magĩcooka muoyo. Andũ angĩ nao nĩmaregire kũrekererio, makĩnyariirwo nĩgeetha makaariũkio magĩe na muoyo mwega makĩria.
English: Women received their dead by resurrection.* Others were tortured, not accepting their deliverance, that they might obtain a better resurrection.

Kikuyu: Andũ angĩ nĩmanyũrũririo na makĩhũũrwo na iboko, o na angĩ makĩohwo na mĩnyororo na magĩikio njeera.
English: Others were tried by mocking and scourging, yes, moreover by bonds and imprisonment.

Kikuyu: Nĩmahũũrirwo na mahiga; o na magĩatũranio na thoo maita meerĩ; ningĩ makĩũragwo na hiũ cia njora. Maathiiaga mehumbĩte njũa cia ngʼondu na cia mbũri, na marĩ ngĩa, na makanyariirwo, o na magekagwo ũũru;
English: They were stoned.* They were sawn apart. They were tempted. They were slain with the sword.* They went around in sheep skins and in goat skins; being destitute, afflicted, ill-treated—

Kikuyu: thĩ ndĩamaagĩrĩire. Moorũũraga werũ-inĩ na irĩma-inĩ, o na ngurunga-inĩ na miungu-inĩ ya thĩ.
English: of whom the world was not worthy—wandering in deserts, mountains, caves, and the holes of the earth.

Kikuyu: Andũ aya othe nĩmagathĩrĩirio nĩ ũndũ wa wĩtĩkio wao, no gũtirĩ o na ũmwe wao wahingĩirio kĩĩranĩro kĩrĩa kĩeranĩirwo.
English: These all, having been commended for their faith, didn’t receive the promise,

Kikuyu: Ngai nĩatũhaarĩirie ũndũ mwega makĩria nĩgeetha andũ acio mati- gatuuo aagĩrĩru ithuĩ tũtarĩ hamwe nao.
English: God having provided some better thing concerning us, so that apart from us they should not be made perfect.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio, kuona atĩ nĩtũrigiicĩirio nĩ aira aingĩ ũguo mahaana ta itu inene-rĩ, nĩtwĩyaũrei kĩrĩa gĩothe gĩtũritũhĩire, o na wĩhia ũrĩa ũtũrigiicaga mũno, na tũgĩtengʼere ihenya rĩrĩa tũigĩirwo mbere iitũ tũkirĩrĩirie.
English: Therefore let’s also, seeing we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, lay aside every weight and the sin which so easily entangles us, and let’s run with perseverance the race that is set before us,

Kikuyu: Nĩtũcũthĩrĩrie Jesũ, ũrĩa mwambĩrĩria na mũkinyanĩria wa gwĩtĩkia gwitũ, ũrĩa nĩ ũndũ wa gĩkeno kĩrĩa aigĩirwo mbere yake-rĩ, nĩoomĩrĩirie kwambwo mũtharaba-inĩ, atekũũria gũconorwo, na rĩu aikarĩte thĩ guoko-inĩ kwa ũrĩo gwa gĩtĩ kĩa ũnene kĩa Ngai.
English: looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising its shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.

Kikuyu: Rĩu-rĩ, cũraniai ũhoro wa ũcio wakirĩrĩirie ngarari nyingĩ ũguo kuuma kũrĩ andũ ehia, nĩgeetha mũtikananoge kana mũũrwo nĩ hinya.
English: For consider him who has endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, that you don’t grow weary, fainting in your souls.

Kikuyu: Inyuĩ mũkĩgiana na mehia-rĩ, mũtirĩ mũrarũa o nginya mũgaita thakame.
English: You have not yet resisted to blood, striving against sin.

Kikuyu: Na nĩmũriganĩirwo nĩ kiugo gĩa kũmũũmĩrĩria kĩrĩa kĩmwaragĩria ta ciana ciake, atĩrĩ: “Mũrũ wakwa, ndũkahũthie irũithia rĩa Mwathani, o na ndũkoorwo nĩ hinya hĩndĩ ĩrĩa egũgũkũũma,
English: You have forgotten the exhortation which reasons with you as with children, “My son, don’t take lightly the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when you are reproved by him;

Kikuyu: nĩgũkorwo Mwathani nĩarũithagia arĩa endete, na akaherithia ũrĩa wothe etĩkĩrĩte atuĩke mwana wake.”
English: for whom the Lord loves, he disciplines, and chastises every son whom he receives.”*

Kikuyu: Inyuĩ kiragĩrĩriai mathĩĩna marĩ taarĩ irũithia; nĩgũkorwo Ngai aramwĩka ũguo ta mũrĩ ciana ciake. Nĩ ũndũ-rĩ, nĩ mwana ũrĩkũ ũtarũithagio nĩ ithe?
English: It is for discipline that you endure. God deals with you as with children, for what son is there whom his father doesn’t discipline?

Kikuyu: Mũngĩkĩaga kũrũithio (na gũtirĩ mũndũ ũtarũithagio), inyuĩ mũkĩrĩ ciana cia mũtumia wa njĩra, no ti ciana ciake.
English: But if you are without discipline, of which all have been made partakers, then you are illegitimate, and not children.

Kikuyu: Ningĩ-rĩ, ithuothe twanakorwo na maithe maitũ marĩa maatũciarire na mũciarĩre wa mwĩrĩ, arĩa maatũrũithagia na ithuĩ tũkamatĩĩa nĩ ũndũ wa ũguo. Tũkĩagĩrĩire kwĩnyiihĩria atĩa Ithe wa maroho maitũ nĩguo tũtũũre muoyo!
English: Furthermore, we had the fathers of our flesh to chasten us, and we paid them respect. Shall we not much rather be in subjection to the Father of spirits and live?

Kikuyu: Maithe maitũ nĩmatũrũithirie gwa kahinda kanini o ta ũrĩa moonaga kwagĩrĩire; no Ngai atũrũithagia tũteithĩke, nĩguo tũgwatanĩre nake ũtheru wake.
English: For they indeed for a few days disciplined us as seemed good to them, but he for our profit, that we may be partakers of his holiness.

Kikuyu: Gũtirĩ irũithia rĩonekaga rĩ rĩega ihinda-inĩ ta rĩu, tiga rĩrĩ rĩa o ruo. No thuutha-inĩ-rĩ, nĩrĩciaraga magetha ma ũthingu na thayũ harĩ andũ arĩa merutaga narĩo.
English: All chastening seems for the present to be not joyous but grievous; yet afterward it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio-rĩ, tambũrũkiai moko manyu marĩa macunjurĩte, na maru manyu marĩa maregeru nĩguo magĩe hinya.
English: Therefore lift up the hands that hang down and the feeble knees,*

Kikuyu: “Rũngariai njĩra cia magũrũ manyu,” nĩgeetha ũrĩa ũthuaga ndakae kuonja, no nĩ kaba ahonio.
English: and make straight paths for your feet,* so what is lame may not be dislocated, but rather be healed.

Kikuyu: Mwĩrutanĩriei mũno gũikarania na andũ othe na thayũ, na gũtuĩka atheru; tondũ hatarĩ ũtheru- rĩ, gũtirĩ mũndũ ũkoona Mwathani.
English: Follow after peace with all men, and the sanctification without which no man will see the Lord,

Kikuyu: Menyererai gũtikagĩe mũndũ o na ũmwe wanyu ũkwaga gũkinyĩrwo nĩ Wega wa Ngai, na mũtigetĩkĩrie ũndũ mũũru ũhaana ta mũri wa mũtĩ mũrũrũ ũkũre thĩinĩ wanyu, ũcooke kũrehe thĩĩna na ũthaahie andũ aingĩ.
English: looking carefully lest there be any man who falls short of the grace of God, lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you and many be defiled by it,

Kikuyu: Tigĩrĩrai nĩmuona atĩ gũtirĩ o na ũmwe wanyu mũhũũri maraya, kana mũndũ ũtetigĩrĩte Ngai ta Esaũ, ũrĩa wendirie igai rĩa ũrigithathi wake nĩ ũndũ wa irio cia irĩa rĩmwe.
English: lest there be any sexually immoral person or profane person, like Esau, who sold his birthright for one meal.

Kikuyu: Thuutha-inĩ, ta ũrĩa mũũĩ, hĩndĩ ĩrĩa eendire kũgaya kĩrathimo gĩake, nĩaregirwo. Ndaahotire kuona kamweke ga kwĩrira, o na gwatuĩka nĩacaririe kĩrathimo kĩu na maithori.
English: For you know that even when he afterward desired to inherit the blessing, he was rejected, for he found no place for a change of mind though he sought it diligently with tears.

Kikuyu: Mũtiũkĩte kĩrĩma-inĩ kĩrĩa kĩngĩhutio, na kĩrĩa kĩraakana mwaki; o kĩu kĩrĩ na nduma, na gĩgathimba, o na kĩrĩ na kĩhuhũkanio;
English: For you have not come to a mountain that might be touched and that burned with fire, and to blackness, darkness, storm,

Kikuyu: ningĩ kũrĩa kũrĩ mũgambo wa coro, o na kana mũgambo waragia na ciugo iria arĩa maaciguire maathaithanire matikaheo ũhoro ũngĩ o na ũmwe,
English: the sound of a trumpet, and the voice of words; which those who heard it begged that not one more word should be spoken to them,

Kikuyu: tondũ matingĩomĩrĩirie ũrĩa gwathanĩtwo, atĩrĩ; “O na nyamũ ĩngĩhutia kĩrĩma kĩu, no nginya ĩhũũrwo na mahiga ĩkue.”
English: for they could not stand that which was commanded, “If even an animal touches the mountain, it shall be stoned”.†*

Kikuyu: Handũ hau haarĩ na ũndũ wa kũguoyohia mũno, ũũ atĩ Musa nĩoigire atĩrĩ, “Nĩndĩrainaina mũno nĩ guoya.”
English: So fearful was the appearance that Moses said, “I am terrified and trembling.”*

Kikuyu: No inyuĩ mũũkĩte Kĩrĩma-inĩ gĩa Zayuni, itũũra inene rĩa Ngai ũrĩa mũtũũra muoyo, na nĩrĩo Jerusalemu ya Igũrũ. Nĩmũũkĩte kĩũngano-inĩ gĩa gĩkeno kĩrĩ araika ngiri na ngiri,
English: But you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to innumerable multitudes of angels,

Kikuyu: kũrĩ kanitha wa marigithathi, arĩa marĩĩtwa mao maandĩkĩtwo kũũrĩa Igũrũ. Mũũkĩte kũrĩ Ngai, ũrĩa mũtuĩri andũ othe ciira, na kũrĩ maroho ma andũ arĩa athingu matuĩkĩte akinyanĩru kũna,
English: to the festal gathering and assembly of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven, to God the Judge of all, to the spirits of just men made perfect,

Kikuyu: na kũrĩ Jesũ ũrĩa mũiguithania wa kĩrĩkanĩro kĩrĩa kĩerũ, o na kũrĩ thakame ĩrĩa yakũminjaminjanĩrio ĩrĩa yaragia kiugo kĩega gũkĩra thakame ya Habili.
English: to Jesus, the mediator of a new covenant,* and to the blood of sprinkling that speaks better than that of Abel.

Kikuyu: Menyererai mũtikarege ũrĩa ũkwaria. Angĩkorwo matiigana gwĩthara hĩndĩ ĩrĩa maaregire ũrĩa wamakaanagia arĩ gũkũ thĩ-rĩ, githĩ ithuĩ tũtingĩkĩaga o makĩria gwĩthara, tũngĩkĩhutatĩra ũrĩa ũtũkaanagia arĩ igũrũ?
English: See that you don’t refuse him who speaks. For if they didn’t escape when they refused him who warned on the earth, how much more will we not escape who turn away from him who warns from heaven,

Kikuyu: Hĩndĩ ĩyo-rĩ, mũgambo wake nĩwainainirie thĩ, no rĩu nĩeranĩire akoiga atĩrĩ, “Ihinda rĩngĩ to thĩ iiki ngainainia, no nĩngainainia igũrũ o narĩo.”
English: whose voice shook the earth then, but now he has promised, saying, “Yet once more I will shake not only the earth, but also the heavens.”*

Kikuyu: Ciugo ici, “ihinda rĩngĩ,” ironania kweherio gwa kĩrĩa kĩngĩenyenyeka, nacio nĩ indo iria ciũmbĩtwo, nĩgeetha kĩrĩa gĩtangĩenyenyeka gĩtũũre.
English: This phrase, “Yet once more” signifies the removing of those things that are shaken, as of things that have been made, that those things which are not shaken may remain.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio tondũ tũramũkĩra ũthamaki ũtangĩenyenyeka-rĩ, nĩtũcookiei ngaatho na tũhooy- age Ngai na njĩra ĩrĩa yagĩrĩire, tũkĩmũtĩĩaga na tũkĩmwĩtigagĩra,
English: Therefore, receiving a Kingdom that can’t be shaken, let’s have grace, through which we serve God acceptably, with reverence and awe,

Kikuyu: nĩgũkorwo “Ngai witũ nĩ mwaki ũniinanaga.”
English: for our God is a consuming fire.
